title: Six-year reporting histories of the 2019 registered population
question: Which available, absent, removed and no-record sequences are most common among 2019 firms, and when do histories break?
notes_text: Source: RFSD v3.1.0; lab aggregation of the foundation registry. The population is firms eligible and registered at year-end 2019 with consistent identity across the release. Each year's state: A, eligible with an original statement; N, eligible, registered, no original; X, recorded registry removal by year-end, which takes precedence over a dissolution-year statement; other, a record that is ineligible or has unresolved registration; blank, no record in that year. A blank after X is expected; a blank without a prior X is not an exit. Rows after the top histories are pooled. FNS era only; no history crosses the provider change. Descriptive; the histories describe the retrieved release, not dated disclosure decisions.
reading: One third of the 2019 registered population reported in all six years. Two in five were absent in 2019, and two thirds of those had a recorded removal by 2024, mostly within one to three years; six percent stayed registered and absent throughout. Histories that break after years of availability (A then N or X) are individually rare but numerous in total.
caveats: FNS era only; no history crosses the provider change
A blank cell after X is expected, a blank without X is not an exit
States describe the retrieved release, not dated disclosure decisions
source_line: Foundation registry 2019-2024, lab pivot of 3,413,062 firms
